requirements.requirement: Configure/identify the private network shared between node1 and node2 (eth1 link) as the path to be shaped.
requirements.summary: eth1 was discovered unconfigured on both nodes, assigned static IPs (192.168.50.1/.2), and bidirectional ping confirmed connectivity before shaping was applied.

requirements.requirement: Limit the throughput node2 obtains through node1 to roughly 1 Mbit/s in each direction.
requirements.summary: tc tbf (root, rate 1mbit) was applied as egress shaper on node1's eth1, and a tc ingress qdisc plus u32 police filter (rate 1mbit, drop) was applied for ingress, covering both directions of the node1-node2 link.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate the ~1 Mbit/s limit with a measured transfer in each direction.
requirements.summary: iperf3 measured node2->node1 at ~1.17/0.92 Mbit/s and node1->node2 (reverse) at ~1.28/0.90 Mbit/s, both consistent with the ~1Mbit/s target in each direction, compared against an unshaped baseline of ~82,000-123,000 Mbit/s on the same link before shaping.

requirements.requirement: Traffic from node1 itself stays unshaped.
requirements.summary: iperf3 from node1 to node3 over the separate br-lan interface (not the shaped eth1) measured ~119 Gbit/s, showing node1's own traffic outside the shaped private link is unaffected. This directly demonstrates node1's traffic on its other network path is not subject to the eth1 shaping rules.

requirements.requirement: Shaping configuration persists across a restart of node1.
requirements.summary: A hotplug script (/etc/hotplug.d/iface/95-shape-eth1) was installed to reapply tc rules on ifup; after a full node1 reboot (boot_id changed a2b75609->7cc764b8, uptime reset to ~27s), the tc qdisc/filter state was confirmed present and a fresh iperf3 transfer still measured ~1.39 Mbit/s, directly showing the healthy pre-restart state, the restart, and recovered shaped behavior.

overall_summary: The executor correctly identified and configured the node1-node2 private link (eth1), applied tc-based egress (tbf) and ingress (police) shaping on node1 at ~1 Mbit/s in each direction, and validated the limit with iperf3 transfers measuring roughly 0.9-1.3 Mbit/s in both directions against a multi-Gbit/s unshaped baseline. Node1's own traffic on its separate br-lan interface was independently measured at ~119 Gbit/s, confirming it remains unshaped. Persistence was demonstrated via a hotplug re-application script and a full node1 reboot showing recovered shaping and boot-identity change. The independent node-restart protocol was run on all three nodes with boot-identity changes confirmed for each; node1 and node2 additionally show recovered shaping/connectivity state post-restart, while node3's restart evidence is limited to a boot-id change and basic connectivity (appropriate since node3 has no shaping-related state).
limitations: node3's restart evidence only shows boot-identity change and a connectivity ping; no service/data-specific recovery check was performed, though node3 has no task-relevant state to verify.

The 'traffic from node1 itself stays unshaped' claim was demonstrated using a different physical path (br-lan to node3) rather than node1-originated traffic on the shaped eth1 device itself; this is a reasonable interpretation of the requirement given the two-node private link topology, but the trace does not show whether node1-to-node2 traffic on eth1 is exempted from shaping (only that node2-to-node1 and node1-to-node2 traffic on that link are both shaped as intended).

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the full chronological command trace. All state-changing commands trace to a clear purpose: eth1 IP configuration and firewall zone creation (prerequisite for the private link), iperf3/tc package installs (prerequisite tooling), tc qdisc/filter application (the core task), the hotplug persistence script (required for durable shaping), and the temporary firewalld port 5201 opening on node3 for the unshaped-traffic test, which was explicitly reverted (cmd-ef0cdde2ffc545af). One tc ingress filter attempt failed (cmd-dfbd85374ca84156, rc=2, 'Failed to load TC action module') due to a missing kernel module; this was corrected by installing kmod-sched-act-police/kmod-ifb (cmd-5ad55a60208040fc) and re-adding the filter successfully (cmd-6ce3a1d0a0414286) — a legitimate troubleshooting-and-fix sequence rather than an abandoned experiment, and it left no residue. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations, no weakened security controls, and no damaged package state were found.
